title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 7-10). Grothendieck has built the isotopy category of oriented combinatorial surfaces. Its morphisms Hom^+_isot(X,Y) are isotopy classes of orientation-preserving embeddings, presented via triples and quadruplets (X,Y,Y',f_0), with Y' a subsurface of Y. On p. 8 he profinitely completes the hom-sets by a contracted product with the profinite completion of the mapping class group: Hom^_isot(X,Y) = Hom_isot(X,Y) ∧^{Γ̂_X}_{Γ_X}. He then defines a composition (13).

Top of this page. Associativity of that composition is 'evident', perhaps obtained by continuity from the discrete pairing. He adds the self-admonition 'Mérite d'être fait avec plus de soin!' ('Deserves to be done more carefully!') and breaks off the concrete construction.

The axiomatic section ('Galois axiomatique'). To replace the ad hoc construction he defines a general framework. A category C is said to have profinite automorphism groups if:
(i) each Aut_C(X) is a profinite group;
(ii) for every u: X→Y, the stabilizer of u in Aut(X)×Aut(Y), under the action u ↦ g u f^{-1}, is a closed subgroup.
Then each Aut(X)×Aut(Y)-orbit in Hom(X,Y) is a homogeneous space G/G_u, a profinite space. Giving Hom(X,Y) the disjoint-union (sum) topology of its orbits makes it locally compact (Hausdorff, totally disconnected).

Composition. He wants the composition (14) Hom(X,Y)×Hom(Y,Z)→Hom(X,Z), (u,v) ↦ vu, to be continuous. It suffices to check this on products of orbits, i.e. for fixed u,v, the map (g,f,g',f') ↦ (g' v f'^{-1})∘(g u f^{-1}). Since this equals g'·v(f'^{-1}g)u·f^{-1}, and Aut acts continuously on each orbit, everything reduces (next page, (15)) to the continuity of φ ↦ vφu from Aut(Y) to Hom(X,Z).

Next page. Let G_u be the stabilizer and H_u = pr_2(G_u) ⊂ Aut(Y). On H_u one has vφu = vuψ, which stays in the orbit of vu and is continuous. The same holds on each coset α_i H_u. Hence continuity follows under hypothesis (16): H_u has finite index, equivalently, being closed, H_u is open.

Purpose. Build an abstract setting, a category enriched in locally profinite spaces whose topology is generated by profinite Aut groups. In it the profinitely completed Teichmüller/isotopy category of surfaces with embeddings is a topological category. This is the stage on which Gal(Q̄/Q), and later its Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type automorphisms, can act.
errors: The claim that composition 'est donc une application continue' is asserted before it is proved. Continuity does not follow from closed stabilizers alone. φ ↦ vφu can meet infinitely many Aut(X)×Aut(Z)-orbits of Hom(X,Z), and the sum topology then breaks continuity. An extra hypothesis is needed, which Grothendieck supplies on the next page as (16): H_u of finite index (= open).

In the parametrization (g,f,g',f') the first factor acts on Y, so the domain should be Aut(Y)×Aut(X)×Aut(Z)×Aut(Y). The manuscript shows an overwritten letter there (Z corrected?), which the transcription renders as Aut(Z).

Associativity of the completed composition is only asserted ('peut-être par continuité'). Grothendieck himself flags it as needing more care. A density argument would work once continuity is established, since the discrete Hom is dense in the contracted product.

ideas.what: Profinite completion of the isotopy category of oriented surfaces with embeddings, via the contracted product Hom ∧^{Γ̂}_{Γ} (preceding page), with composition and associativity by continuity.
ideas.modern_name: Profinite completion of mapping class groupoids / Teichmüller tower including subsurface-embedding morphisms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse, 1984) in outline; developed by Drinfeld, Ihara, Nakamura, Harbater–Schneps, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, Boggi in the 1990s-2000s
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, profinite completions) in outline; no details of this construction

ideas.what: Axiomatic notion of a category 'à groupes d'automorphismes profinis': profinite Aut(X), closed stabilizers of morphisms, Hom-sets topologized as disjoint unions of profinite orbits (locally compact).
ideas.modern_name: Category enriched in locally profinite spaces / topologized Galois-type category; cf. infinite Galois categories with Noohi-type topologies
ideas.usually_credited_to: No single standard source; related to Grothendieck's SGA1 Galois categories and to later infinite Galois theory (Noohi; Bhatt–Scholze 2015)
ideas.where_published: Not in SGA1 in this form; possibly unpublished

ideas.what: Criterion for continuity of composition: the image H_u of the stabilizer G_u in Aut(Y) must be open, i.e. of finite index; continuity is checked on cosets α_i H_u.
ideas.modern_name: Openness condition ensuring a topological category structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard point-set argument; not specifically credited

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches a general axiomatic framework ('Galois axiomatique') of categories whose hom-sets get a locally profinite topology induced by profinite automorphism groups of the objects. The intended model is the profinitely completed category of surfaces with isotopy classes of embeddings, not just a groupoid. He marks the construction as needing more care and leaves it unfinished.
missed.quote: Mérite d'être fait avec plus de soin! ... Galois axiomatique Une catégorie C est dite "à groupes d'automorphismes profinis" si pour tout X ∈ C, Aut X est muni d'une structure de groupe profini
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The published Teichmüller-tower literature mostly works with profinite groupoids, plus separate inclusion maps between mapping class groups. A topological category with genuine embedding morphisms and hom-topology governed by Aut-actions is a cleaner setting for GT-type actions. It sits near modern infinite Galois categories (Bhatt–Scholze, Noohi), though that link is not made explicitly in the literature as far as I know.

deep.surprise_reason: A tidy, not fully standard axiomatization of profinite-topologized categories with non-invertible morphisms, aimed at the Teichmüller tower. It is interesting as an early (≈1978-81) precursor of the Esquisse framework. Mathematically it is mostly point-set routine, and its spirit is absorbed into later profinite-groupoid treatments.
transcription_corrections: Domain of the last displayed map: the first factor appears overwritten (Z → Y?). The mathematics requires Aut(Y)×Aut(X)×Aut(Z)×Aut(Y).

'sont des espaces homogènes quotients' is better read as: orbits become (profinite) homogeneous quotient spaces. Hom(X,Y) is then endowed with the sum topology of the profinite topologies of the orbits.
'Je veux que l'accouplement des morphismes (14) ... soit [est] donc une application continue': 'morphisme' and 'continue' are struck, replaced by 'une application continue'.
'on se voit que' is likely 'on se ramène à voir que' / 'il suffit de voir que' (illegible). The inserted phrase 'pour u,v fixés' modifies the claim about 'l'application'.

Struck passage: '[-opérant par Aut_C(Y) (opérant à gauche) et à droite)-]' corresponds to a deleted description of the left/right action. The retained text is 'les stabilisateurs dans Aut_C(X)×Aut_C(Y) de u ∈ Hom_C(X,Y) [action u ↦ g u f^{-1}] sont des sous-groupes fermés'.
